A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HiP attention work despite the changed title and expanded serving framework. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support matching retained, revised, and added material.

before.justification: v1 reports original language-modeling, MMLU, LongBench, BookSum, multimodal, latency, and ablation results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 reports original PG19, passkey, RULER, LongBench, BookSum, multimodal, offloading, and attention-locality results, alongside retained experiments.

M1.justification: The hierarchical pruning backbone remains, but v2 changes branch representatives from first tokens to center tokens and introduces strided sampling within blocks. Section 3.3 adds separate GPU hot-token caches and vector/hash page tables, substantially extending v1's preliminary UVM offloading. Appendix C.4 also integrates HiP with SelfExtend.

E1.justification: v2 adds PG19, passkey retrieval, RULER, and Arxiv healing data. Its multimodal evaluation replaces ChartQA and InfoVQA with MME cognition/perception while retaining MMMU, DocVQA, GQA, and TextVQA (v1 Table 9; v2 Table 8). WikiText2, MMLU, LongBench, and BookSum remain represented.

E2.justification: Beyond v1's principal StreamingLLM and HyperAttention comparisons, v2 evaluates A, AVD, BigBird, and H2O in the main benchmark suite. BigBird also joins the MMLU and multimodal comparisons. Reformer and SEA remain in the corresponding appendix experiment; these additions are evaluated comparators, not merely citations.

E3.justification: The main evaluations switch from LLaMA2/Qwen models to Llama3.1-8B and separately test sparse prefill, sparse decoding, and both phases. BookSum introduces 32k–128k books, 2k-token summaries, an 8k-token GPU-cache budget, and window-size controls. Healing and latency settings also change, including the new 500-step Arxiv recipe and expanded offloading configurations.

E4.justification: v2 adds empirical checks of attention-locality assumptions, a neighboring-token patch study, representative-token-position ablations, SelfExtend configuration studies, and sorting-removal experiments on RTX 4090/H100. The mask-refresh analysis is revised under different benchmarks. Earlier block-size, dense-layer, ensemble, and summary-case analyses are substantially retained and relocated.

E5.justification: v2 introduces substantial statistical estimation absent from v1's corresponding analysis: fitted attention-score-difference distributions, distance-dependent means and standard deviations, correlation estimates, Gaussian-fit KL divergence, and logarithmic-fit NRMSE (Appendix A.3). These characterize the proposed stochastic model. Benchmark run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, and significance tests remain unreported.

E6.justification: Many earlier multi-model results are replaced by Llama3.1 measurements, with additional retrieval, context-extension, and offloading outcomes. For example, v2 Table 5 reports 6.83× decoding speedup at 128k with 96.0% relative LongBench performance, and Table 6 reports 95.45 tokens/s with vector-map offloading at 64k on RTX 4090. These are new-setting results, not direct improvements over v1's speedups. The Reformer/SEA perplexities remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v1 provides algorithm equations and complexity reasoning without comparable correctness theorems. v2 Section 4 and Appendix A introduce probabilistic attention-locality assumptions, lemmas, derivations, and proofs supporting center-token selection over random selection in a simplified top-1 setting, plus a conditional optimality theorem.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction expand the contribution from a training-free sparse attention mechanism to a serving framework addressing algorithmic cost, GPU computation, and memory management. New central claims concern a mathematical advantage over random pruning and offloading with O(log T) GPU-resident tokens. The training-free hierarchical attention contribution is retained.

C2.justification: v2 develops attention locality as the mechanism explanation and discusses nonzero means, correlated score differences, and failure of the independence approximation near the final pruning iterations. It explicitly identifies missed top-k tokens through early branch termination, qualifies vector-map versus hash-map memory/latency trade-offs, and analyzes hardware-dependent slowdowns. These substantially extend v1's limitations discussion.

D1.justification: A new reproducibility statement describes supplementary code, kernel and evaluation entry files, configuration classes, and serving integrations. v2 also documents FlashAttention versions, offloading memory limits, weight/cache precision, and the Arxiv healing recipe. Some earlier healing details disappear, but the new implementation and execution information is substantial.

R1.justification: v2 adds connections to MInference/SnapKV-style attention, SelfExtend/YaRN, SGLang, and newer models and benchmarks, while removing some earlier citations. The central positioning relative to StreamingLLM, HyperAttention, and SEA remains largely intact and is mostly moved to Appendix E.1.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, and introduction are extensively rewritten around three serving objectives. The document adds a theory section and reproducibility statement, reorganizes the experiments and appendices, shortens main-text related work, and moves MMLU and multimodal evaluation into the appendix. This is substantial narrative restructuring.

P2.justification: The introductory and method diagrams are redrawn, several radar-chart presentations become tables, and main comparisons use color-coded tables grouped by prefill/decoding configuration. New offloading schematics, latency breakdowns, memory-throughput plots, and statistical figures substantially change the visual presentation. Several earlier appendix plots are retained and relocated.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the previously limited evidence for effective long-context retrieval and practical memory offloading. Passkey/RULER tests, phase-specific comparisons against more baselines, measured offloading trade-offs, and detailed execution instructions make the central claims more assessable. These gains outweigh narrower main-model coverage. The theory remains conditional and simplified, and the logarithmic-space hash-map variant does not deliver the vector-map variant's throughput; the added discussion makes these limits visible.
